name: Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct
notes: TWO-PART MODEL. (1) Vision: custom 32-layer ViT, hidden_size 1280, 16 heads, patch_size 14, spatial_merge_size 2, temporal_patch_size 2, out_hidden_size 3584. No windowed attention in Qwen2-VL (full attention over all patches). (2) LLM: Qwen2-7B dense decoder, 28 layers, hidden 3584, 28 heads / 4 KV heads, head_dim 128 (verified: k_proj weight is [512, 3584] = 4*128). ARCHITECTURE = dense, because the LLM backbone is dense. CONTEXT_SCALING = mrope: rope_scaling.type is literally 'mrope' with mrope_section [16,24,24] (t,h,w interleaved across 64 of the 128 head-dim halves), so positions are 3-D, not 1-D. VISION TOKENS: dynamic resolution, no fixed grid. tokens = (H/28)*(W/28) because patch 14 merges 2x2. A 448x448 image = 16*16 = 256 vision tokens. DOMINANCE: vision does NOT dominate at typical resolutions -- a 256-token image against a ~1000-token text prompt puts text at ~80% of prefill. But cost is attacker-controlled via image size: a 4K image (3840x2160) is 137*77 = 10,549 vision tokens, which completely dominates. KV CACHE: 28 layers * 4 kv_heads * 128 head_dim * 2 (K and V) * 2 bytes (bf16) = 57,344 B/token (= 56 KiB). At 32,768 ctx that is 1.75 GiB of resident KV per sequence. FLOPs_per_token_active = 2 * 8.291e9 = 1.66e10 for the LLM decode step only; the vision encoder is a one-time ~0.6B-param forward pass per image that this per-token figure does not capture. params_b 8.291 = HF API safetensors total (8,291,375,616), not the '7B' in the name -- the vision tower plus the 152,064-row embedding table account for the difference.
